concepts.title: Keeping the Neighbourhood Clean
concepts.description: Understanding the importance of hygiene, waste disposal, and maintaining greenery in the surrounding area.
key_ideas: Throwing garbage in dustbins
Keeping parks and streets clean
Planting trees and caring for plants
Avoiding the use of plastic bags

concepts.title: Emergency Services
concepts.description: Identifying critical services required during accidents, fires, or theft and knowing how to contact them.
key_ideas: Role of the Police Station and Police Officers
Role of the Fire Station and Firefighters
Role of Hospitals and Ambulances
Important emergency telephone numbers

concepts.title: Being a Good Neighbour
concepts.description: Learning the social values and etiquette required to live peacefully and happily within a community.
key_ideas: Helping neighbours in need
Celebrating festivals together
Not making loud noise or disturbing others
Greeting and respecting elders in the neighbourhood

concepts.title: Safety in the Neighbourhood
concepts.description: Basic safety rules to follow when walking, playing, or interacting with others in the neighbourhood.
key_ideas: Walking on the footpath
Using zebra crossings
Playing in parks, not on the road
Stranger safety awareness

concepts.description: Importance of Plants — part of the chapter on Plants and Trees.
key_ideas: Core principles of importance of plants
Step-by-step problem solving for importance of plants
Real-world applications of importance of plants

concepts.title: How Plants Grow — Seed to Plant
concepts.description: How Plants Grow — Seed to Plant — part of the chapter on Plants and Trees.
key_ideas: Core principles of how plants grow
Step-by-step problem solving for how plants grow
Real-world applications of how plants grow

concepts.title: Parts of a Plant
concepts.description: Identification and functions of different parts of a plant including roots, stem, leaves, flowers, and fruits.
key_ideas: Roots hold the plant in the soil
Stems carry water and food
Leaves make food for the plant
Flowers grow into fruits

concepts.title: Types of Plants: Trees, Shrubs, and Herbs
concepts.description: Classifying plants based on their size and stem structure, distinguishing between big trees, bushy shrubs, and small herbs.
key_ideas: Trees have hard, thick woody stems called trunks
Shrubs are smaller than trees and have woody stems
Herbs are very small plants with soft, green stems

concepts.title: Climbers and Creepers
concepts.description: Understanding plants with weak stems that need support to grow upright or grow along the ground.
key_ideas: Climbers need support like a stick or wall to grow up
Creepers grow along the ground because their fruit is heavy
Both have weak stems compared to trees

concepts.title: Parts of Plants We Eat
concepts.description: Identifying which specific parts of different plants are used as food, such as eating the root of a carrot or the leaf of spinach.
key_ideas: We eat roots like carrots and radishes
We eat stems like sugarcane and potato
We eat leaves like spinach and cabbage
We eat seeds like rice and wheat

concepts.title: Things We Get From Plants
concepts.description: Exploring non-food items provided by plants that are useful in daily life, such as materials and medicines.
key_ideas: Plants give us wood for furniture
We get cotton and jute for clothes
Some plants provide medicines (like Tulsi and Neem)
Flowers are used to make perfumes

concepts.description: Habitats — Land, Water, Air — part of the chapter on Animals and Birds.
key_ideas: Core principles of habitats
Step-by-step problem solving for habitats
Real-world applications of habitats

concepts.title: What Animals Eat
concepts.description: What Animals Eat — part of the chapter on Animals and Birds.
key_ideas: Core principles of what animals eat
Step-by-step problem solving for what animals eat
Real-world applications of what animals eat

concepts.title: Wild and Domestic Animals
concepts.description: Distinguishing between animals that live in the forest and animals that live with humans or on farms.
key_ideas: Wild animals live freely in nature without human help
Domestic animals are kept by humans for work or food
Pets are animals kept inside homes for companionship

concepts.title: How Animals Move
concepts.description: Exploring the different ways animals travel from one place to another using specific body parts.
key_ideas: Birds and insects use wings to fly
Fish use fins and tails to swim in water
Land animals use legs to walk, run, or hop
Snakes and worms crawl or slide on the ground

concepts.title: Animal Shelters and Homes
concepts.description: Identifying specific names of natural and man-made homes where different animals live and sleep.
key_ideas: Natural homes include dens, burrows, and nests
Man-made homes include sheds, stables, and coops
Animals need homes to protect themselves from heat, cold, and rain

concepts.title: Animals and their Young Ones
concepts.description: Learning the specific names given to the babies of different animals.
key_ideas: Different animals have specific names for their babies (e.g., cow and calf)
Some babies look like their parents, while others look different
Birds lay eggs which hatch into young ones

concepts.title: Things We Get From Animals
concepts.description: Understanding the utility of domestic animals and the products humans derive from them.
key_ideas: Farm animals provide food like milk, eggs, and honey
Animals provide materials like wool, silk, and leather
Some animals like donkeys and oxen help humans carry loads

concepts.title: Caring for Animals
concepts.description: Developing empathy and learning how to treat animals with kindness and respect.
key_ideas: Animals need food, water, and love just like humans
We should not tease or hurt animals
Sick or injured animals need medical help from a vet

concepts.title: Uses of Water
concepts.description: Uses of Water — part of the chapter on Water and Air.
key_ideas: Core principles of uses of water
Step-by-step problem solving for uses of water
Real-world applications of uses of water

concepts.title: Importance of Clean Air
concepts.description: Importance of Clean Air — part of the chapter on Water and Air.
key_ideas: Core principles of importance of clean air
Step-by-step problem solving for importance of clean air
Real-world applications of importance of clean air

concepts.title: Sources of Water
concepts.description: Identifying where water comes from, distinguishing between natural sources like rain and rivers, and man-made sources like taps and wells.
key_ideas: Rain is the main source of water.
Water is found in lakes, ponds, rivers, and seas.
We get water at home through taps, wells, and handpumps.

concepts.title: Properties of Air
concepts.description: Understanding the basic characteristics of air through simple observation and feeling, even though it cannot be seen.
key_ideas: Air is all around us, but we cannot see it.
We can feel air when it moves.
Air takes up space (like inside a balloon).

concepts.title: Clean Drinking Water
concepts.description: Learning why we must drink clean water to stay healthy and simple methods to make water safe for drinking.
key_ideas: Dirty water contains germs that can make us sick.
We should boil or filter water before drinking.
Drinking water should be stored in covered containers.

concepts.title: Moving Air: Wind
concepts.description: Defining wind as moving air and recognizing how it helps us in daily life and nature.
key_ideas: Moving air is called wind.
A gentle wind is called a breeze; strong wind is a storm.
Wind helps dry clothes, move sailboats, and fly kites.

concepts.title: Saving Water
concepts.description: Understanding the value of water and identifying good habits to avoid wastage in daily activities.
key_ideas: Water is precious and should not be wasted.
Close the tap while brushing teeth.
Reuse water used for washing vegetables to water plants.

concepts.title: Road Safety Rules
concepts.description: Road Safety Rules — part of the chapter on Safety.
key_ideas: Core principles of road safety rules
Step-by-step problem solving for road safety rules
Real-world applications of road safety rules

concepts.title: Safety at Home
concepts.description: Safety at Home — part of the chapter on Safety.
key_ideas: Core principles of safety at home
Step-by-step problem solving for safety at home
Real-world applications of safety at home

concepts.title: Safety at School
concepts.description: Learn about safe behavior within the school premises, including classrooms, corridors, and staircases.
key_ideas: Do not run in the corridors or on stairs
Do not push or pull others
Do not jump on desks or chairs
Use a sharpener instead of a blade to sharpen pencils

concepts.title: Safety in the Playground
concepts.description: Understanding how to play safely with friends and use playground equipment without getting hurt.
key_ideas: Wait for your turn at swings and slides
Do not stand in front of a moving swing
Follow the rules of the game
Do not fight while playing

concepts.title: Safety in the Bus
concepts.description: Rules to follow while waiting for, boarding, and travelling in a school bus or public vehicle.
key_ideas: Stand in a queue while boarding the bus
Do not put your head or hands out of the window
Do not disturb the driver
Get down only when the bus stops completely

concepts.title: Safety while Swimming
concepts.description: Essential precautions to take when going for a swim or playing near water bodies.
key_ideas: Never go swimming alone; always go with an adult
Use a swimming tube or floaters if you are learning
Do not run near the pool edge
Do not push others into the water

concepts.title: First Aid Basics
concepts.description: Introduction to the immediate help given to an injured person before proper medical help arrives.
key_ideas: Inform an adult or teacher immediately if someone gets hurt
Do not crowd around the injured person
Wash small cuts or wounds with clean water
Understanding the First Aid box
